subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.**

Jimmy danced his way to glory, laughing all the way to the bank __after winning the trophy__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **No substitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The underlined segment "laughing all the way to the bank after winning the trophy" is **grammatically correct** and appropriate in the given context.
 
• The original sentence, "*Jimmy danced his way to glory, laughing all the way to the bank after winning the trophy,*" is idiomatic and doesn't require any substitution.
 
• It effectively conveys the idea that Jimmy celebrated his victory and success by dancing happily, and this led to financial gains (hence, "laughing all the way to the bank").
 
• The sentence is both grammatically and conceptually correct, so **no substitution** is needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 1**
